judged_text: deleteEvent's fallback searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, making the `event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)` fallback provably dead code that always returns undefined. Cancelling bookings whose reference carries no externalCalendarId now calls Google's events.delete with an undefined calendarId, so the event is never removed from the destination calendar and remains orphaned, where the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback deleted it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback branch), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId` (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), which cannot match the real destination calendar externalId in normal cases, so the fallback returns `undefined`. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single DC), so this is a concrete regression that will prevent deleting from the intended destination calendar when the reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.
